transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we all know, we're here to review the legal launch checklist for the voice-authentication access system rollout in six weeks. Per our fixed process, I'll be recording each of your reports in order. Marcus, you're up first — please give your substantive report covering the required checklist fields: affected population, consent or labor restrictions, vendor-data restrictions, and the concrete document or implementation action required. Once I've recorded yours, we'll move to Dana, then Owen. Let's get started.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I reviewed the current employee roster and state-law matrix this week, and I confirmed that exactly 620 Illinois employees will be enrolled in this system. Illinois biometric law requires written opt-in consent before collecting their voiceprints, and it also requires the company to publish a retention schedule. These two points are not currently in the rollout approval memo, so they need to be addressed before we can proceed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my labor findings. I reviewed the applicable collective bargaining agreement and confirmed two key restrictions: first, employee voice monitoring is prohibited outside working hours; second, the union must receive exactly 14 calendar days' advance notice before covered employees are enrolled. I should note that the labor checklist has not yet been updated with these requirements.

transcript.text: I need to share my information-security findings. I confirmed with the vendor's security team that the standard configuration retains raw voiceprints for 365 days and permits secondary analytics use. The vendor will amend the agreement to delete voiceprints within exactly 30 days and prohibit secondary use, but that amendment has not yet been requested in the legal approval package.

commitments.detail: Update the rollout approval memo to include written opt-in consent requirement for 620 Illinois employees and publish a retention schedule before enrollment begins.
Update the labor checklist to reflect the prohibition on voice monitoring outside working hours and the requirement to provide the union with 14 calendar days' advance notice before enrollment.
Request the vendor amendment in the legal approval package to require deletion of voiceprints within 30 days and prohibit secondary analytics use.

All three checklist updates must be completed and submitted for final legal approval before the six-week rollout date. Union notice must be given no later than 14 calendar days before any covered employee is enrolled.
